newsitem.title: USA: Latin debts perk up, Russia jumps on rating hopes.
newsitem.headline: Latin debts perk up, Russia jumps on rating hopes.

text.p: Latin Bradies extended their recent rally, powered by rising U.S. Treasuries. An influx of institutional money boosted Russian loans in anticipation of credit rating on its first Eurobond issue, traders said.
"The Latins are very strong," said a Brady bond trader. Whatever little profit-taking that had chipped the gains in the last few days was over, while fresh buying kept nudging prices higher, he said.

The winning streak of Latin Bradies in the recent rallies has shrunk their spreads over Treasuries to almost the level of their price peak in 1993/1994, said a head emerging market debts trader at a U.S. bank.
"There's not much head room left," he said.

The advance today alone squeezed the spreads tigher by about 20 basis points for Brazil C, which jumped 1-3/8 to 67-7/8, Venezuela DCB, which climbed 1-1/8 to 79-7/8 and Argentina FRB, which gained 1-1/8 to 82.00.
Yield-seekers were making forays into Nigeria, Moroco, and poised to re-enter in Ecuador and Bulgaria, the trader said.
Bulgaria came under renewed selling in Europe as some investment banks issued negative assessments of the country's precarious economy, traders said.
"It boils down to your believing if the IMF would pull the rug under Bulgaria," said the first trader.
The International Monetary Fund delayed the disbursement of aid because Bulgaria failed to make adequate progress in structural reforms.
Russia participation loans soared on strong institutional buying, said the second trader.
Optimism that Russia would get a double-B rating on its first Eurobond issue fuelled the rally, he noted, adding Vnesh loans were better bid than Minfins, he added.
Russia dollar Vnesh rose a whopping 1-7/8 to 64-3/4. The best performing Min Fin 4 and Min Fin 5 each added 1.00 full point to 49-3/4 and 33.00.
